solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Romantic drive? Look around in the same place

indicators.note: around tells us the word for look is wrapped about the next piece

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
ibid is the Latin abbreviation used in footnotes for in the same place

explanation.surface: A lover is told to glance about the very spot they stand in search of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: IBID (from ibidem) is a footnote convention; LO goes round it to give LIB-IDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire, the drive behind romance, with the question mark owning that it is a loose sense.

clue.text: Friend rose on the football side — a real flier

indicators.note: rose in a down clue says the friend word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a wing is a side of a football pitch, or a winger's position

explanation.surface: A friend climbed up on the football flank, a real high-flyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like a flower or a past tense: it reverses PAL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bird, the plover also called peewit, so it genuinely flies.

clue.text: Analysis of collapse

definitions.meaning: a detailed itemised account, as of costs
a failure or ..., as of health or machinery

explanation.surface: An analysis of a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an itemised account of figures and a sudden failure in health or machinery.

clue.text: Pretty fastidious

definitions.meaning: fussy, particular about food or manners

explanation.surface: Pretty reads as 'rather', so the clue seems to say someone is quite fussy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means delicately attractive and also fussy or particular in taste.

clue.text: Good bowling, and no runs for captain

parts.note: in cricket an over is a spell of six balls bowled
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket report: tight bowling, nothing conceded, praise for the skipper.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER in cricket is a set of six deliveries from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal titles for the person in charge, the boss or chief who gives the orders.

clue.text: Forget to order vermouth

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Someone neglects to ask the bartender for a vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and It is a British cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out or neglect it is to forget it.

clue.text: State of a hot pie I ordered

indicators.note: ordered says the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A customer describes the condition of the hot pie they ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition but means a country.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an independent country in the Horn of Africa, a nation state.

clue.text: Norwegian with a choice of directions

indicators.note: with lets the choice word sit among the compass letters

parts.note: N and SE are the compass points north and south-east
or is the word that offers a choice

explanation.surface: A Norwegian traveller with several routes to choose from.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read N OR SE: north or south-east, a choice of directions.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for the old Scandinavian people and their language, so it stands for Norwegian.

clue.text: Castle on Eastern Railway is a bird's nesting place

parts.note: a rook is the chess piece also called a castle

explanation.surface: A castle on an eastern rail line houses a colony of nesting birds.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a colony of rooks, the crows that nest together in treetops.

clue.text: Title to settle beforehand

definitions.meaning: an honorific placed before a name, such as Dr or Mrs
to fix or arrange something in advance

explanation.surface: Choosing a form of address in advance of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A title such as Sir is a word put in front of a name, and pre-fixing something is arranging it ahead.

clue.text: At one time a chart-topper with other arrangement

parts.note: a chart-topping record is a hit

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters of other reorders them

explanation.surface: A number one single once came out in a different musical arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' looks musical but turns OTHER into HERTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning up to that point or previously, it refers to an earlier period, so it loosely stands for formerly.

clue.text: Bound for Rouen, perhaps, with a note

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters of the French city may be shuffled

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A traveller headed for Rouen, with a note in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase meaning on the way, so travelling towards somewhere, as bound for does.

clue.text: Wells included with writers in this case

definitions.text: Wells included with writers in this case

parts.words: Wells included with writers in this case
parts.note: the wells are inkwells and the writers are pens, both held on a desk stand; the surface suggests H. G. Wells among authors

explanation.surface: The novelist H. G. Wells is counted among the writers in this instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk stand holds inkwells and pens together, so it is the case that contains wells along with writing implements.

clue.text: The commanding officer must get present, to be consistent

parts.note: CO is the military abbreviation for commanding officer
present in the sense of in attendance, here

explanation.surface: An officer in charge insists on being in attendance so as not to seem inconsistent.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold together logically or stick together as a unified whole is to be consistent.

clue.text: Stagger to us and collapse

indicators.note: collapse tells us the letters of to us and fall apart into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone staggers towards us and falls down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagger' looks like reeling but means amaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to amaze or stun them, a close synonym.

clue.text: Midnight quarrel to develop

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night is G
a row is a noisy argument or quarrel

explanation.surface: A late-night argument escalates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' is read as the middle of 'night', its central letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Developing and getting bigger or maturing are the same process, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Plot links prisoners to criminal activity

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts, prisoners
piracy is robbery at sea or illegal copying, a criminal activity

explanation.surface: A scheme ties inmates to a crime wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret plan by a group to do something unlawful is a plot.

clue.text: Like to be sure, so find out

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as
being certain is being sure

explanation.surface: Someone who wants to be certain makes enquiries.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something for certain by investigation is to find it out.

clue.text: Ivor's out to become a skilled performer

indicators.note: to become says the letters of Ivor's and out turn into something new

explanation.surface: Ivor is out to make himself an accomplished performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'to become' does the reordering.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician or other artist of outstanding technical skill is a virtuoso performer.

clue.text: Firm belief in guilty verdict

definitions.meaning: a firmly held opinion or certainty
a court's formal finding that someone is guilty

explanation.surface: A juror's firm belief in a guilty verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a strongly held certainty and the legal act of finding someone guilty of an offence.

clue.text: A reaper in the fall

definitions.meaning: one who crops or harvests a crop
a heavy fall, as in to come one

explanation.surface: A harvester at work in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' suggests the American autumn but means a tumble, as in to come a cropper.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means someone who harvests crops and, idiomatically, a heavy fall or failure.

clue.text: Wound bringing endless panic

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the panic word is cut off

parts.note: a scare is a sudden panic

explanation.surface: An injury caused by a moment of terror that never seems to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The mark left by a healed injury, so it stands for the wound itself or its trace.

clue.text: Feel regret about changing the side's balance

indicators.note: about tells us the regret word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to rue is to feel regret

indicators.note: changing says the letters of side are rearranged

parts.note: side's is side plus 's, the 's being link material: side gives its letters

explanation.surface: A captain regrets reshuffling the team's balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balance' looks like the team's poise but means what is left over; the 's of side's is surface glue.
explanation.definitionFit: What remains after the rest is used up is the balance, a remainder.

clue.text: Pang suffered by one of two, for example, on rising

parts.note: a twin is one of a pair

indicators.note: on rising in a down clue says the example abbreviation is read upwards

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A sudden pang felt by one twin, for instance on getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp pain or emotional stab is a pang.

clue.text: Do get up to tidy around a curiosity

indicators.note: get up says the little word do is turned to read upwards, backwards
around here means the letters of tidy are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to rise and tidy up the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get up' is the reversal signal in an across clue, and 'around' here means shuffled rather than surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strange or peculiar, a curio, is an odd thing, a curiosity.

clue.text: Runaway debtor in a mess

parts.note: DR is the bookkeeping abbreviation for debtor

indicators.note: a mess here means the letters of in a are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fugitive debtor in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runaway' looks like a fugitive but is a channel water runs away down.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe or channel carrying waste water off is a way for it to run away, a cryptic gloss.

clue.text: Girl was about to enter without warning

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

indicators.note: to enter means the about word goes inside was

parts.note: re is Latin for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A girl was on the point of coming in without anyone being told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to enter' reads as 'on the point of coming in', but 'about' is the Latin-derived abbreviation and 'to enter' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught off guard means being taken by surprise, an idiom for without warning.

clue.text: An island heaven, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us the heaven word is only heard, not spelt

parts.note: the sky is the heavens

explanation.surface: A traveller calls an island paradise heaven on earth.
explanation.walkthrough: SKYE is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large island off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: They're much smarter than their mates

definitions.text: They're much smarter than their mates

parts.words: They're much smarter than their mates
parts.note: smarter means more showily dressed, not cleverer: the male birds have the gorgeous tails, the peahens are drab

explanation.surface: Some people are much cleverer than their friends.
explanation.definitionFit: The males of the species have brilliant fan tails while the females are plain, so they are better turned out than their partners.

clue.text: Admitted to part of hospital — mental perhaps

parts.note: a patient admitted to hospital is in
a ward is a room or section of a hospital

explanation.surface: Someone taken into a psychiatric unit of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mental' looks like a kind of ward but is the definition, as in inner thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental processes happen inside the mind, so they are internal; 'perhaps' marks this as one example.

clue.text: Held in remand perhaps, so paid for release

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of remand and so are one possible rearrangement

explanation.surface: A prisoner held on remand, and so money was handed over to free them.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage freed by a payment has been bought back, which is exactly being paid for to secure release.

clue.text: Irishman goes to church meeting to seek spiritual guidance

parts.note: Sean is a common Irish man's name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irishman goes to a church gathering looking for religious advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting where people try to contact the dead is a gathering seeking messages from spirits.
